key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, moderate thermal gradients and stabilize axial forces in HDPE joining.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defect formation.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combined simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive reliability beyond the tested HDPE welding parameter space remains unestablished.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
